newsitem.title: POLAND: Poland invites bids for paper maker Swiecie.
newsitem.headline: Poland invites bids for paper maker Swiecie.

text.p: The Polish privatisation ministry invited bids for up to 75 percent in Poland's leading paper maker Zaklady Celulozy i Papieru w Swieciu Celuloza SA (Celuloza Swiecie), the ministry said in a newspaper announcement.
It said it wanted to sell Celuloza Swiecie's shares in blocks of no less than 10 percent and set the deadline for the bids for October 28.
It said it earmarked 20 percent of the firm's shares for employees and five percent for a government programme to compensate former owners for property confiscated under communism.
The Swiecie, northern Poland, company which employs 3,250 has a 25-percent market share in Poland and netted 110 million zlotys on sales on 1.1 billion zlotys in 1995.
It expects to net 102 million zlotys on similar sales this year.
The ministry earlier said it wanted to float the company and list it on the Warsaw Stock Exchange in the first quarter of 1997, after finding a strategic investor for the firm.
